- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently under-estimates price spikes in the 1–3 day horizon after strong sentiment shifts; add 0.5–1.5x the spike magnitude to forecast.
- Model over-estimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0x the recent average deviation.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 → +0.67), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7x the recent 7-day average to forecast.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; apply 1.2x the recent 5-day slope to forecast.
